lines.text: Nvidia's Nemotron language model has thirty billion parameters, but uses only about three billion for each word.
Normal models get slower and need more memory as the text gets longer, because they keep checking everything before.
lines.title: The problem

lines.text: Mamba layers keep a small running summary, like notes. A few attention layers can still look back at earlier words.
lines.title: Two kinds of layers

lines.text: Mixture of experts: the model has 128 small experts, and a router picks just six for each word.
lines.title: 6 of 128 experts

lines.text: Smaller numbers shrink the model from about sixty-six gigabytes to about twenty-two.
lines.title: Smaller storage

lines.text: It also guesses several words ahead, and the main model checks the guesses in one pass.
lines.title: Speed trick

lines.text: AI agents call a model dozens of times per task, so cheaper answers make them more practical.
lines.title: Takeaways
